facts.fact: Biometric Update reports that the government has implemented a pilot in about 40 councils in partnership with OpenCRVS as part of civil registration digitisation; no date is given for the pilot, so the document's published date is used.

The mayor of Njombe-Penja council (Littoral) says his staff are being prepared for training to migrate from handwritten to digital birth certificates, with BUNEC's support, so certificates there are still handwritten; undated, so the document's published date is used.

A BUNEC official says a 2025-2029 strategic plan for civil registration is being elaborated, to launch in 2025 and reach a fully digital system by 2029; it follows the PAMEC support programme, whose second phase began in 2021 and was due to end in 2024.

In July 2024 Cameroon signed a US$4.8 million grant agreement with Korea through KOICA for civil registration digitisation; the 2025-2029 plan is supported by Vital Strategies and the Bloomberg Philanthropies Data for Health Initiative.

The pilot is described as implemented by the government, with the National Civil Registration Office (BUNEC) supporting councils in the move to digital certificates; undated, so the document's published date is used.
